rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so round 2 pushes obfuscation intensity up while respecting the program's profile: Olden power is a small (5354-byte text, 18 functions), compute-bound workload whose hot functions (Compute_Tree, Compute_Branch, Compute_Lateral, optimize_node) sit in tight recursive traversals, so the runtime-heavy passes BCF and FLA get SecurityGain-led weights (0.7) with restrained RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights (0.4-0.5) so they concentrate on high-value functions rather than spraying every basic block, whereas cheap, low-risk passes SUB and SPLIT get uniformly high weights (0.6-0.8) to be applied broadly and raise static-analysis cost across the whole binary at minimal overhead. IBR, ICALL, and IGV are held at moderate, balanced weights: indirect branching and indirect calls pair well with FLA to hide the flattened dispatcher structure, and IGV obscures the program's global grid state, but their per-call/per-access overhead argues against aggressive weighting in this loop-dominated code. All seven passes remain enabled to maximize layering and structural diversity; correctness risk is tolerable since round 1 showed a clean build and run with no ICE fallback, leaving headroom for this harder configuration.
